incidents.victim: Oil & gas, healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, and logistics firms (Warren Oil, Maxxis International-USA, Newpark Resources, Quantum Health, and ~24 others)
incidents.vector: Social engineering: callers posed as IT help desk staff to trick employees into giving up login credentials or installing remote access tools, then deployed ransomware.
incidents.impact: A 60-plus-member network with ties to the former Conti gang extorted at least 28 companies for a combined $40.5 million; Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, arrested four alleged leaders and seized cash and devices, but say the wider network remains at large.

incidents.victim: Unnamed organizations running VMware vCenter Server
incidents.vector: After exploiting a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, the actor moved laterally to an internal Linux appliance and used a custom Golang tool ("BONESAW") to exploit a new VMware vCenter zero-day (CVE-2026-123890) and forge SSO administrator access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant/GTIG disclosed full compromise of vCenter environments via a previously unknown vulnerability, with credential theft, SAML token forgery, and data exfiltration from compromised appliances; Broadcom has released patches.

incidents.vector: Attackers used the open-source ARTEX AI hacking platform to breach Commission systems beginning around Oct. 22, 2026.
incidents.impact: Payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements, and translation services were disrupted for more than 10 days; the Commission found no evidence of a broad staff data breach or ransom demand, but the investigation remains open.

incidents.victim: Rocket Mortgage LLC and Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage)
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees on phone calls to trick the company's IT help desk into issuing temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication to access systems.
incidents.impact: A 2023 breach exposed large amounts of private customer information; NY DFS fined Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper a combined $6.75 million for MFA and late-incident-reporting failures.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians and law enforcement officials
incidents.vector: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information of high-profile European officials, continuing a long-running DDoS and doxing campaign against supporters of Ukraine.
incidents.impact: Victims included Italy's Foreign Minister, Europol's Cybercrime Centre head, and German journalists; the EU separately sanctioned the group and 24 individuals tied to a related Russian influence-operations firm.

incidents.victim: American victims of Southeast Asian scam compounds
incidents.vector: Scam-compound operators in Cambodia and Burma ran virtual-currency investment fraud schemes against Americans and Europeans, protected by armed groups including the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army.
incidents.impact: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned scam-center operator Zhao Hui, two affiliated companies, and DKBA commanders for facilitating cyber-enabled investment fraud targeting U.S. citizens.

incidents.victim: Employees of an unnamed Silicon Valley technology and defense company
incidents.vector: A Russian national recruited via Telegram entered the U.S. illegally, used fraudulent identification and electronic surveillance equipment, and conducted in-person surveillance and stalking of company employees.
incidents.impact: DOJ indicted Igor D'iu for acting as an unregistered Russian agent targeting a company supplying weapons used in Ukraine; he faces up to 10 years in prison and remains in federal custody.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to two of Japan's national supercomputers.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included registered-user details, research data from home directories, and SSH keys used to connect the supercomputers to outside services.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a third-party vendor that provides SharePoint data-migration services to Infoblox and stole customer data from it.
incidents.impact: Cybersecurity firm Infoblox is notifying customers of the breach; the number of affected customers and whether extortion was involved have not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations including CNN, BBC, Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, GitLab, and NPR
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform (dubbed "OPTIMJACK") to inject malicious JavaScript into customers' sites, served from Optimizely's own trusted CDN.
incidents.impact: The malware swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, stole cookies and screenshots, and pushed Coruna/DarkSword iOS exploit kits; roughly $7,500 in cryptocurrency was confirmed stolen before Optimizely patched the flaw and removed the code.

incidents.victim: 700+ French supermarkets, butchers, food factories, and a slaughterhouse
incidents.vector: Iran's IRGC Cyber-Electronic Command (Shahid Kaveh unit) hacked commercial refrigeration controllers, causing units to fail.
incidents.impact: Spoiled stock caused tens of millions of euros in losses across French retailers; French officials formally attributed the October attack to Iran and are pushing the EU for sanctions.

incidents.victim: U.S. hospitals, schools, and healthcare providers (6+ states)
incidents.vector: The "8-Digits Team," affiliated with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations, gained network access, exfiltrated data, and extorted victims under threat of releasing stolen records.
incidents.impact: The group claimed more than 50 terabytes of data including 70 million-plus health records and made over $500 million in ransom demands; a Kazakh national was extradited from Italy to face U.S. charges carrying up to 27 years in prison.

incidents.victim: Two unnamed US-based organizations (government, defense-contractor, and NGO-adjacent)
incidents.vector: The group compromised a cloud productivity environment using stolen Super Admin credentials and an MFA fatigue attack, then reused stolen contact data and impersonation pretexts to phish a second organization via a compromised federated identity account.
incidents.impact: The group exfiltrated entire cloud drives, email archives, and employee rosters, and maintained persistence for months using rogue passkeys and MFA backup codes; Mandiant assesses the group remains an active threat with new phishing operations observed as recently as November 2026.

incidents.victim: Cursor (5,000 potential users) and Uber (149,346 individuals), among other Fireworks/Notion customers
incidents.vector: A financially motivated group exploited a leaked access key at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks to steal credentials and session data, then used stolen credentials to tamper with Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace and to access a third-party cloud storage bucket tied to Uber.
incidents.impact: Attackers inserted a malicious Claude Code extension available for about 11 hours, and separately exposed names, addresses, and driver's license images for 149,346 Uber-related individuals; the activity is linked to a broader "LLMjacking" campaign also affecting Notion.

incidents.victim: Government organizations across Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe
incidents.vector: The group has used two previously undocumented remote access trojans, PerfectPioneer RAT and KUKURAT, with covert HTTP/3 (QUIC) command-and-control channels since at least mid-2025.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports high-stealth, long-term intelligence-collection operations against government targets with capabilities designed specifically to evade detection tooling; the campaign remains active, with the group's tooling still evolving as of early 2026.

incidents.victim: Indian defense contractors and military personnel (with potential global defense-sector targeting)
incidents.vector: Hackers possibly aligned with the Pakistani government built realistic fake job-recruiter websites impersonating major defense firms to trick job seekers into downloading GravityRAT spyware.
incidents.impact: Lookout found the year-long, still-active campaign stealing contacts, call logs, texts, and WhatsApp messages from victim devices, with tactics that could extend beyond India to defense personnel globally.

incidents.vector: A newly identified group has been hacking telco infrastructure and planting backdoors that run malicious SS7 and Diameter signaling commands.
incidents.impact: The backdoors let the group collect device data, track subscriber locations, and intercept calls and SMS traffic on carefully selected targets; the group has been active for at least two years.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across internal and other cloud environments.
incidents.impact: The attacker had access to Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days before being detected and removed; the company has since revoked the exposed key.
